policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads 'Simon Peter' (Simon = Sigma-iota-mu-omega-nu), and the mapped textual_variant note relegates the other reading to the margin: 'Many ancient authorities read Symeon.' The note marks Symeon as what the ASV did not print, so the text renders r01.

ASV text reads 'called us by his own glory and virtue': the possessive 'his own' renders the adjective idia with the datives, i.e. the base reading. The mapped textual_variant note puts the rival in the margin ('Some ancient authorities read through glory and virtue' = dia doxes kai aretes), confirming the base is the printed text.

ASV 'his precious and exceeding great promises' keeps timia before megista, which excludes r01 (megista kai timia, 'exceeding great and precious'). It does not distinguish where hemin stands: 'he hath granted unto us' renders the pronoun the same whether it follows megista (base) or timia (r02). No note bears on the unit; the one note here is alternative_rendering.

The unit is the presence or absence of the article to with the following noun; English 'the corruption that is in the world by lust' would read identically either way, and Greek anarthrous nouns of this kind are regularly rendered definite. No mapped textual note; the single note is alternative_rendering and cannot decide a reading.

hamartematon and hamartion are synonyms both rendered 'sins'; ASV 'the cleansing from his old sins' is the same English for either. The only note is alternative_rendering ('Or, closing his eyes') and concerns a different word.

ASV 'I shall be ready always to put you in remembrance' renders the future mello ('I shall be about/ready to'). The rival ouk amelesa/ouk ameleso is a litotes, 'I will not be negligent to put you in remembrance'; the ASV shows no negative and no verb of negligence, so it renders the base.

ASV 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased' is the fixed English order for this saying and does not report where houtos estin stood in the Greek; nor does collapsing 'my Son, my beloved' into 'my beloved Son' reveal whether the second mou was present. The only note is a greek_gloss on 'having received'.
Both readings say 'in the holy mount'; the difference is attributive order and the extra article (hagio orei vs orei to hagio), which English cannot show. No note is attached to the verse.
The unit is only the order of prophecy and pote; ASV 'For no prophecy ever came by the will of man' renders either arrangement identically. The verse's single note is a greek_gloss on 'was brought'.

ASV reads 'but men spake from God': 'from God' renders the preposition apo with theou, the base reading. The rival substitutes hagioi, yielding 'holy men of God spake'; the ASV has no 'holy' with 'men' here, reserving 'Holy' for the Spirit, so it renders the base.
